# InditexTech Karate Tools

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/

Karate Tools is a toolkit for teams testing REST APIs with [Karate](https://docs.karatelabs.io). It scaffolds a new Karate module from a Maven archetype, generates test scenarios, data sets and mocks straight from an Open API definition, and ships ready-to-use clients for the databases and messaging systems your tests need to talk to.

- **One archetype, one command** — a working Karate project, configured and ready to run.
- **Tests you don’t have to write** — Open API in, Gherkin scenarios and mocks out.
- **Clients included** — JDBC, MongoDB, Kafka and JMS, ready to use in tests.

Karate Tools is developed in the open at InditexTech, and built for teams to actually use — bug reports, fixes and new features are all welcome.

[Star the repository on GitHub](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss)

## Frequently asked questions

Have more questions? Open an issue — we’ll respond as quickly as possible.

Is Karate Tools free and open source?

Yes. Karate Tools is distributed under the Apache 2.0 License: you can use, modify and distribute it, including in commercial applications.

Do I need an Open API definition to use Karate Tools?

No. The Open API generator is optional — the archetype gives you a working Karate project either way; the generator just saves you from writing scenarios, test data and mocks by hand when a definition exists. See [Open API generator](main/guides/open-api-generator/overview/).

Do I need to write Java to use Karate Tools?

Mostly no — tests are plain Karate `.feature` files and YAML/JS configuration. Java is only involved if you extend the clients or generators themselves. See the [quickstart](main/quickstart/).

Can I use Karate Tools outside InditexTech?

Yes — Karate Tools is public open-source software, usable by anyone under the Apache 2.0 License.

# About Karate Tools

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/about/

Karate Tools is a toolkit to facilitate a Karate module’s initialization, configuration, test generation and execution.

⚙️ **Initialization** and **configuration** through a Maven archetype.

🗂️ **Automated generation** of test scenarios, test data and external services mocks from Open API.

🛠️ Usual operations such as **authentication**, **database interaction**, and **messaging (Kafka & JMS)**.

⏩ **Execution** in different environments of Karate tests for a REST artifact.

## Key features

Using an archetype (`karatetools-archetype`), Karate Tools generates a Karate project from scratch with the necessary configurations and utilities for the generation and execution of Karate tests.

- **Configuration files** (karate, auth, jdbc, kafka, …​).
- **JavaScript and Karate utilities**, which include: - the management of files and payloads. - authentication (basic, JWT, …​), allowing you to change from one to another via the test configuration. - initialization and management of Karate mock servers for external services.
- **Java dependencies** to the `karatetools-starter`, which include: - `open-api-generator`, a Java command-line interface for the automatic generation of tests in Gherkin, with their related data sets and schemas for response validation, as well as data to mock external services from Open API definitions. See [Karate Open Api Generator](../guides/open-api-generator/overview/). - Java clients to interact with relational databases (JDBC), a non-relational database (MongoDB), event messaging (Kafka consumer and producer) and JMS messaging. See [Karate Clients](../guides/clients/overview/). - a Java `KarateCache` to share variables across tests. See [Karate Cache](../guides/execution/karate-cache/).

## Benefits

- **Faster onboarding:** a new module starts from a working, opinionated structure instead of a blank project.
- **Less boilerplate:** Open API generation removes most of the manual work of writing scenarios, test data and mocks by hand.

## What Karate Tools is not

- Karate Tools does not replace [Karate](https://docs.karatelabs.io) itself — it is a set of conventions, generators and clients built on top of it.

## Status and roadmap

Karate Tools is actively maintained and used internally at InditexTech; this site tracks its current, stable feature set. See the [release notes](../release-notes/overview/) for what changed recently.

## Overview

The high-level architecture of Karate Tools is shown in the following diagram:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Project structure

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Karate Tools Archetype](../guides/archetype/overview/) | Archetype to initialize a Karate Maven project from scratch with all its dependencies. |
| [Karate Tools Open API Generator](../guides/open-api-generator/overview/) | Automatic generation of tests in Gherkin, with their related data sets and schemas for response validation, as well as data to mock external services from Open API definitions. |

For the repository’s own module-by-module breakdown (the code that implements Karate Tools itself, as opposed to the modules a Karate Tools user works with), see [Contributing > Development](../development/).

# Contributing

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing-overview/

Thank you for your interest in contributing to this project! We value and appreciate any contributions you can make.

## Ways to contribute

- **Report a bug** — open an issue in our [issue tracker](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/issues).
- **Suggest a feature** — open an issue explaining your idea.
- **Contribute code** — read the [development guide](../development/) and follow [the step-by-step guide](../contributing/step-by-step/) below.

## Before you start

- [Contribution guide](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Code of conduct](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [License](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/blob/main/LICENSE)
- Before starting to contribute to the code, you must first sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA) — see [the CLA instructions](https://github.com/InditexTech/foss/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Contribution guidelines

- All contributors are expected to follow the project’s code of conduct. Please be respectful and considerate towards other contributors.
- Before starting work on a new feature or fix, check existing [issues](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/issues) and [pull requests](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/pulls) to avoid duplication.
- If you wish to work on an existing issue, comment on it to let other contributors know you’re on it.
- Discuss and gather feedback from the community before making significant changes to the project’s structure or architecture.
- Keep a clean, organized commit history — divide changes into logical, descriptive commits.
- Sign off your commits (`Signed-off-by`) to comply with the DCO: - use `git commit -s` (or `git commit --signoff`) on each commit, or - enable it repository-wide: `git config commit.signoff true`.
- Document any new changes or features you add.
- Link the corresponding issue in your pull request.
- Add license and copyright information following the [REUSE specification](https://reuse.software/spec/#copyright-and-licensing-information) — this repository uses [REUSE.toml](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/blob/main/REUSE.toml) to manage it.

## How to contribute

1. Open an issue to discuss and gather feedback on the feature or fix you wish to address.
2. Fork the repository and clone it to your local machine — see [GitHub Docs - Fork a repository](https://help.github.com/en/github/getting-started-with-github/fork-a-repo).
3. Create a new branch to work on your contribution: `git checkout -b your-branch-name`.
4. Make the necessary changes in your local branch: - implement the new feature or fix; - follow the established project style and formatting guidelines; - test your changes to ensure they don’t introduce errors; - update documentation as needed — see the [development guide](../development/).
5. Make clear, descriptive, signed-off commits that explain your changes.
6. Push your branch: `git push origin your-branch-name`.
7. Open a pull request describing your changes and linking the corresponding issue. Automated verification checks run on every pull request — unit, mutation, integration and Karate tests, each with its own coverage threshold.
8. Await review comments and make any necessary changes.
9. Once approved, your contribution is merged into the `develop` branch and included in the next release.

# Development

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/development/

This page explains the process of implementing new features or fixing bugs in the Karate Tools ecosystem, and points you at the [repository structure](../contributing/repo-structure/overview/) and the [step-by-step guide](../contributing/step-by-step/). For the contribution process itself (issues, pull requests), see [Contributing](../contributing-overview/).

## Development process

The steps to follow are:

- Implement the new feature or fix the bug.
- Perform the necessary tests: - create or update the corresponding **unit tests**, execute them, and verify that they pass and that the code coverage is over the established threshold (90%); - execute the **mutation tests**, verify that they pass and that the mutation coverage is over the established threshold (90%); - create or update the corresponding **integration tests**, execute them, and verify that they pass and that the code coverage is over the established threshold (80%); - create or update the corresponding **Karate tests**, execute them, and verify that they pass and that the code coverage is over the established threshold (80%).
- Update the relevant documentation.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The [repository structure](../contributing/repo-structure/overview/) page describes the code structure, to help you find the location of the code to add or modify, how to execute and verify the tests, and how to update the documentation.

## Environment setup

See [Prerequisites](../prerequisites/) for the tools and versions required, and [the docs module](../contributing/repo-structure/docs/) for how to build this documentation site locally.

## Testing

See each [repository module](../contributing/repo-structure/overview/)'s own page for its testing instructions — unit and mutation tests for the `code` modules, integration tests in `karatetools-oss-boot`, and Karate tests in `karatetools-oss-karate-test`.

Once you’re ready, follow the [step-by-step guide](../contributing/step-by-step/) to submit your contribution.

# Prerequisites

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/prerequisites/

This page lists what you need before using Karate Tools. After meeting these requirements, follow the [quickstart](../quickstart/).

## Tool requirements

1. [Git](https://git-scm.com/about)
2. [asdf](https://asdf-vm.com/guide/getting-started.html) (version management)

The required asdf plugins and versions are defined in the repository’s own `.tool-versions` file. The current required versions are:

- `maven 3.9.14`
- `java temurin-25.0.3+9.0.LTS`

## Minimum checklist before starting

- Tool requirements above are met.
- The target project to be tested with Karate Tools exists, and at least runs locally.
- You know in which artifact the project’s REST Open API is defined — and the Open API of any external services you want to mock.

# Quickstart

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/quickstart/

In this quickstart, you scaffold a new Karate module from the archetype and run its first test. Before you begin, make sure you meet the [prerequisites](../prerequisites/).

## Step by step

To set up a Karate project for testing a REST artifact, follow these steps:

1. Ensure the [prerequisites](../prerequisites/) are met.
2. Run the [archetype](../guides/archetype/overview/) to set up the initial Karate project.
3. Follow the [configuration](../reference/configuration/overview/) steps.
4. Generate tests, data sets and mocks from Open API definitions with the [Open API generator](../guides/open-api-generator/overview/).
5. Integrate [Karate clients](../guides/clients/overview/) in the tests for test data preparation and test validation.
6. Follow the [execution](../guides/execution/overview/) instructions: running, reporting, starting a local application and other utilities (KarateCache, …​).

## Examples in this repository

The Karate Tools repository includes working examples for each of the areas above, under `e2e/karate/src/test/resources`:

```
e2e/karate/src/test/resources
└── com
    └── inditextech
        └── karate
            ├── auth
            ├── base
            ├── clients
            │   ├── db
            │   │   ├── JDBCClient-MariaDB.feature
            │   │   ├── JDBCClient-PostgreSQL.feature
            │   ├── jms
            │   │   └── JMSClient-ActiveMQ.feature
            │   ├── kafka
            │   │   └── KafkaClients.feature
            │   └── mongodb
            │       └── MongoDBClient.feature
            └── karatetools-openapi-test
                └── xxx-api-rest-stable
                    ├── functional
                    │   └── e2e
                    │       ├── e2e.feature
                    │       └── test-data
                    └── smoke
                        └── BasicApi
                            ├── createItems
                            │   ├── createItems.feature
                            │   └── test-data
                            ├── listItems
                            │   ├── listItems.feature
                            │   └── test-data
                            └── showItemById
                                ├── showItemById.feature
                                └── test-data
```

# Step by step

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/step-by-step/

This section provides a step-by-step guide to contributing to the Karate Tools.

It is intended to help you get started with the project and to provide you with a clear path to follow as you work on your contribution.

## karatetools-oss

### Identify

| 1. Create a `Feature Request` or `Bug Report` Issue in GitHub using the repository templates. [https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/issues/new/choose](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/issues/new/choose) The issues are labeled according to their type: - `kind/feature`: a need to be covered, new functionalities or requests for specific features - `kind/bug`: functional or technical incident in the karate tools For example: - `[Karate-Tools] RabbitMQ Support` - `[Karate-Tools] ActiveMQ - Missing Fields in Message` | ![steps kt oss github issue types](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-issue-types.png) ![steps kt oss github issue examples](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-issue-examples.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Create a new branch from the `develop` branch for the new feature or bug fix with the following naming convention: `<feature or bugfix>/GH-XXX-short-description`. For example: - `feature/GH-1-rabbitmq-support` - `bugfix/GH-2-activemq-missing-fields` | ![steps kt oss github branches](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-branches.png) |

### Implement

| 1. Implement the corresponding **code changes**. For example: 1. `karatetools-oss-clients` - Add the `RabbitMQClientFactory` class. - Add the instantiation of the `RabbitMQClientFactory` class to the `JMSClientFactory`. 2. `karatetools-oss-archetype` - Add the client property (`includeJMSClient_RabbitMQ`) in `archetype-metadata.xml` file. - Add the `configuration template` for the `rabbitmq` client in the `archetype-resources` folder. - Add the generation logic in the `archetype-post-generate.groovy` file. 3. …​ | ![steps kt oss new jms client factory](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-factory.png) ![steps kt oss new jms client config](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-config.png) |
| --- | --- |

### Test

#### Unit

| 1. Implement **unit** tests to verify the corresponding `codebase`. For example: 1. `karatetools-oss-clients` - Add the `unit tests` for the affected classes. - Execute the `unit tests` to ensure that **code works as expected** - Verify the corresponding code is properly **covered** by those tests (**`JaCoCo coverage >= 90%`**). - Execute the `mutation tests` to ensure that the **unit tests are robust enough** (**`mutation coverage >= 90%`**). 2. `karatetools-oss-archetype` - Add the `archetype project test(s)` for the new client. - Execute the `archetype tests` to ensure that the affected **template configurations are properly generated**. - *This type of tests do not generate coverage nor require mutation tests*. 3. …​ | ![steps kt oss new jms client ide unit tests](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-ide-unit-tests.png) ![steps kt oss new jms client ide coverage](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-ide-coverage.png) ![steps kt oss new jms client ide mutation](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-ide-mutation.png) ![steps kt oss new jms client ide mutation report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-ide-mutation-report.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Execute all the codebase `unit tests` in the new branch using the `maven` command: - `mvn clean verify -DskipITs -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false` - `mvn surefire-report:report-only -DalwaysGenerateSurefireReport=true` - Verify **all tests pass** (`code/target/reports/surefire-report.html`) and the code coverage generated by unit tests (`code/jacoco-report-aggregate/target/site/jacoco-aggregate/index.html`) is at least **90%**. | ![steps kt oss unit surefire report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-unit-surefire-report.png) ![steps kt oss unit jacoco report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-unit-jacoco-report.png) |

#### Mutation

| 1. Execute all the codebase `mutation tests` in the new branch using the `maven` command: - `mvn clean verify pitest:mutationCoverage pitest:report-aggregate-module -DskipITs` - Verify **all tests pass** and the mutation coverage generated by mutation tests (`code/target/pit-reports/index.html`) is at least **90%**. | ![steps kt oss mutation report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-mutation-report.png) |
| --- | --- |

#### Integration

| 1. Implement **integration** tests to verify the corresponding `codebase`. For example: 1. `karatetools-oss-boot` - Add the `rabbitmq` `docker` image in the `docker-compose.yml` test file. - Update the `DockerHealthControllerIT` test to include the `rabbitmq` expected service. - Add the `integration tests` for the affected classes. - Execute the `integration tests` to ensure that the **code works as expected when integrated** with the new docker service. 2. …​ | ![steps kt oss new jms client ide integration tests](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-ide-integration-tests.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Execute all the codebase `integration tests` in the new branch using the `maven` command: - `mvn clean verify -DskipUTs -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false` - `mvn surefire-report:failsafe-report-only -DalwaysGenerateSurefireReport=true` - Verify **all tests pass** (`code/target/reports/failsafe-report.html`) and the code coverage generated by integration tests (`code/jacoco-report-aggregate/target/site/jacoco-aggregate-it/index.html`) is at least **80%**. | ![steps kt oss integration failsafe report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-integration-failsafe-report.png) ![steps kt oss integration jacoco report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-integration-jacoco-report.png) |

#### Karate

| 1. Implement **karate** tests to verify the corresponding `codebase`. For example: 1. `karatetools-oss-karate-test` - Add the `karate tests` for the affected classes (config and feature files). - Execute the `karate tests` to ensure that the **code works as expected as part of a karate module**. 2. …​ | ![steps kt oss new jms client ide karate tests](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-ide-karate-tests.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Execute all the codebase `karate tests` in the new branch following the steps defined in - [Karate local execution (no code coverage)](../repo-structure/karate-test/#karate-local-execution). - [Karate local execution with code coverage](../repo-structure/karate-test/#karate-local-execution-with-code-coverage). - Verify **all tests pass** and the code coverage generated by karate tests (`target/jacoco-e2e/index.html`) is at least **80%**. | ![steps kt oss karate karate report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-karate-karate-report.png) ![steps kt oss karate jacoco report](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-karate-jacoco-report.png) |

### Document

| 1. Implement the corresponding **documentation**. For example: 1. `jms-providers.adoc`: Add the new `Rabbit MQ` client to the list of supported JMS providers. 2. `jms-config-rabbbitmq.adoc`: Document the configuration properties for the `Rabbit MQ` client. 3. …​ | ![steps kt oss new jms client documentation](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-documentation.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Launch the `documentation` locally to ensure that the **documentation is properly generated** following the steps defined in: - [Documentation local build](../repo-structure/docs/#docs-local-build). | ![steps kt oss new jms client documentation local](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-new-jms-client-documentation-local.png) |

### Commit

| 1. Make clear and descriptive commits that explain the changes implemented in the new branch and push them to the repository. - Sign off your commits (`Signed-off-by`) to comply with DCO requirements. - Use `git commit -s` (or `git commit --signoff`) to add the trailer to each commit. - Or enable it automatically for this repository: `git config commit.signoff true`. | ![steps kt oss github commit](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-commit.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Make sure the change is reflected in the **Unreleased** section of the `code/CHANGELOG.md` file, categorized according to the type of change implemented. - **Added** for new features. - **Changed** for changes in existing functionality. - **Deprecated** for soon-to-be removed features. - **Removed** for now removed features. - **Fixed** for any bug fixes. - **Security** in case of vulnerabilities. For example: ``` ## [Unreleased] ### Added - [#XXX](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/issues/XXX) To be completed ### Fixed - [#YYY](https://github.com/InditexTech/karatetools-oss/issues/YYY) To be completed ``` | ![steps kt oss github changelog](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-changelog.png) |

### Pull Request

| 1. Create a `Pull Request` from the new branch to the `develop` branch. - `unit`, `mutation`, `integration` and `karate` tests will be executed automatically. - The `Pull Request` will be blocked if any of the tests fail or the coverage is below the defined thresholds. 2. Await comments and discussions on the pull request. Make any necessary modifications based on the received feedback 3. Once the pull request is approved, the contribution will be merged into the develop branch. - The merge strategy to use is **`Squash and merge`** | ![steps kt oss github pull request checks blocked](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-pull-request-checks-blocked.png) |
| --- | --- |

### Release

| 1. Create the release pull request 1. Once all issues are addressed and merged into `develop`, create a pull request from `develop` branch to `main` using corresponding label: - `release-type/major`: Defines the version as a major increment (x+1.y.z). - `release-type/minor`: Defines the version as a minor increment (x.y+1.z). - `release-type/patch`: Defines the version as a patch increment (x.y.z+1). 2. Documentation is versioned separately - see the `docouture-docs-versioning` skill (`docs/.release-version` + the `docs/release` label on its own pull request) rather than a label on this code release pull request. | ![steps kt oss github release pull request](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-release-pull-request.png) ![steps kt oss github release labels](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-release-labels.png) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Wait for the release preview to finish - The preview contains the proposed version number and the list of changes to include in the CHANGELOG. - If the CHANGELOG is not updated, the release preview will fail. | ![steps kt oss github release preview](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-release-preview.png) |
| 1. Merge the release pull request - If the release preview is correct, you can merge the pull request. - The merge strategy to use is **`Create a merge commit`** - The merge will trigger the release workflow. | ![steps kt oss github release workflow](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-release-workflow.png) |
| 1. Merge the sync pull request(s) - The merge strategy to use is **`Create a merge commit`** - Release changes and preparation for the next iteration are now coming to `develop` in a sync pull request (`Sync release X.X.X to develop`) | ![steps kt oss github sync pull request](../../_images/contributing/steps-kt-oss-github-sync-pull-request.png) |

# Reference

# Karate Tools Migration Guide

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/release-notes/migration-guide/

## Karate Tools Migration to 6.0.0 - JDK 25

To migrate to 6.0.0, the following changes must be applied:

- `.tool-versions`: - `maven 3.9.4` to `maven 3.9.14` - `java temurin-21.0.4+7.0.LTS` to `java temurin-25.0.3+9.0.LTS`
- `pom.xml`: - Update java version properties: - `<maven.compiler.source>25</maven.compiler.source>` - `<maven.compiler.target>25</maven.compiler.target>` - `<java.version>25</java.version>` - Update karate-tools version property: - `<karatetools.version>6.0.0</karatetools.version>` - Update testing plugins version properties: - `<maven-surefire-plugin.version>3.5.6</maven-surefire-plugin.version>` - `<maven-surefire-report-plugin.version>3.5.6</maven-surefire-report-plugin.version>` - Update build plugins version properties: - `<maven-dependency-plugin.version>3.11.0</maven-dependency-plugin.version>` - `<exec-maven-plugin.version>3.6.3</exec-maven-plugin.version>` - `<maven-compiler-plugin.version>3.15.0</maven-compiler-plugin.version>` - Add the following property and plugin configuration to the `pom.xml`: ``` <properties> ... <!-- Maven Enforcer Plugin --> <maven-enforcer-plugin.version>3.6.3</maven-enforcer-plugin.version> </properties> <build> <plugins> ... <!-- Maven Enforcer Plugin --> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId> <version>${maven-enforcer-plugin.version}</version> <executions> <execution> <id>enforce-versions</id> <phase>validate</phase> <goals> <goal>enforce</goal> </goals> <configuration> <rules> <requireMavenVersion> <version>[3.9.14]</version> </requireMavenVersion> <requireJavaVersion> <version>[25,26)</version> </requireJavaVersion> </rules> </configuration> </execution> </executions> </plugin> </plugins> ```

# Archetype module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/archetype/

> What is Archetype? In short, Archetype is a Maven project templating toolkit. An archetype is defined as an original pattern or model from which all other things of the same kind are made.

The `karatetools-oss-archetype` module povides the templates and scripts to generate **karate-test** modules.

This module has the following structure:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

It includes the following files:

```
code/archetype/
├── pom.xml
└── src
    ├── main
    │   └── resources
    │       ├── META-INF
    │       │   ├── archetype-post-generate.groovy (1)
    │       │   └── maven
    │       │       └── archetype-metadata.xml (2)
    │       └── archetype-resources (3)
    │           ├── .gitignore (4)
    │           ├── .tool-versions (5)
    │           ├── pom.xml (6)
    │           └── src
    │               └── test
    │                   ├── java
    │                   │   └── KarateRunnerTest.java (7)
    │                   └── resources
    │                       ├── config (8)
    │                       │   ├── db
    │                       │   │   ├── mariadb-config-local.yml
    │                       │   │   ├── mongodb-config-local.yml
    │                       │   │   └── postgresql-config-local.yml
    │                       │   ├── jms
    │                       │   │   └── activemq-config-local.yml
    │                       │   └── kafka
    │                       │       └── kafka-config-local.yml
    │                       ├── config-local.yml (9)
    │                       ├── config.yml (9)
    │                       ├── jwt
    │                       │   └── default-jwt.yml (10)
    │                       ├── karate-config.js (11)
    │                       ├── logback-test.xml (12)
    │                       └── mocks
    │                           └── templates
    │                               └── standalone (13)
    │                                   └── .gitkeep
    └── test
        └── resources
            └── projects (14)
                ├── all (15)
                │   ├── archetype.properties (16)
                │   ├── goal.txt (17)
                │   └── reference (18)
                │       ├── .gitignore
                │       ├── .tool-versions
                │       ├── pom.xml
                │       └── ...
                ├── default (15)
                │   ├── archetype.properties (16)
                │   ├── goal.txt (17)
                │   └── reference (18)
                │       ├── .gitignore
                │       ├── .tool-versions
                │       ├── pom.xml
                │       └── ...
                ...
```

| **1** | **post-processing script** to **choose** the **files** to **include** based on the **archetype properties** which are prompted to the user. |
| --- | --- |
| **2** | **archetype descriptor**, metadata defining the **archetype properties**, **files** and **directories**, and the **post-processing script**. |
| **3** | the **prototype files** that are copied by the archetype plugin to the target module |
| **4** | **prototype**: Git ignore file |
| **5** | **prototype**: Tools version manager file |
| **6** | **prototype**: Karate pom file |
| **7** | **prototype**: Java Test Runner |
| **8** | **prototype**: karate clients configuration files templates |
| **9** | **prototype**: Configuration Files (general and environment specific) |
| **10** | **prototype**: Karate Authentication Default JWT |
| **11** | **prototype**: Karate-config file |
| **12** | **prototype**: logback configuration file |
| **13** | **prototype**: karate mocks folder to define standalone mock templates |
| **14** | **test projects** to test the archetype generation with different configurations |
| **15** | **test**: project folder |
| **16** | **test**: archetype properties (groupId, artifactId, version, …​) |
| **17** | **test**: maven goal to be executed for the project test, for example: `clean validate` |
| **18** | **test**: expected output files |

> **Important**
> Any changes made in the prototype files and/or processing scripts must be reflected in the corresponding output project tests.

# Boot module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/boot/

The `karatetools-oss-boot` module includes the following packages:

- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate`: **Spring Boot Application**
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.config`: **Spring Boot Application configuration**
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.controller`: **Spring Boot Application controllers** implementing the **Open API** test specification and **docker containers** to be used as target for the **karate tools tests** (runner, rest, auth, jdbc, mongodb, kafka, jms, …​). The controller package includes the following classes: - `BasicApiController.java`: Controller implementing the **Open API test specification**. - `DockerHealthController.java`: Controller to check the status of the **docker containers**.

The docker containers are defined in the `docker-compose.yml` file and are started automatically when the application is started.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The `karatetools-oss-boot` module includes all the **integration tests** for the **karate tools**.

> **Important**
> Any changes made in the Karate Tools **codebase** must be reflected in the corresponding **integration tests** in this module, both as **java tests** and as **karate scenarios** (when applicable).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

---

# Clients module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/clients/

The `karatetools-oss-clients` module includes the following **core** and **support** packages.

The **core** packages are:

- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.db`: **JDBC client** to interact with **relational databases**. The included drivers are: - 🛢️ MariaDB - 🛢️ PostgreSQL
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.mongodb`: **MongoDB client** to interact with **MongoDB**.
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.kafka`: **Kafka clients** to interact with **Kafka**.
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.jms`: **JMS client** to interact with **JMS**. The included clients are: - ✉️ Active MQ Artemis - ✉️ Rabbit MQ

The **support** packages are:

- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.logging`: **logging** utilities to **log** the **clients** methods.
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.parser`: **parser** utilities to **parse** the **clients** configuration files and inject system properties.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Code

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/code/

The following sections will describe the **code structure**, to be able to **find easily the location of the code to be added or modified**.

- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-archetype](../archetype/)
- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-clients](../clients/)
- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-generators](../generators/)
- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-runner](../runner/)
- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-starter](../starter/)
- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-boot](../boot/)
- 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-openapi-test](../openapi-test/)

The tests to be executed for the `code` modules are:

- **Unit & Mutation Tests**: - Unit tests are used to test the classes and methods of the `code` modules. - Mutation tests are used to verify that the unit tests are effective.
- **Integration tests**: - Integration tests are used to test the `code` modules together with external dependencies. - These tests are supported by a set of `docker containers` located in `code/src/test/resources/compose`

> **Important**
> Unit, mutation and integration tests are required as status checks in the CI/CD pipeline pull request approval process. The **level of coverage for each type of test must reach at least the defined threshold**.

> **Note**
> Karate tests are defined in the `e2e/karate` folder and are executed in the `karatetools-oss-karate-test` module.

Table 1. Tests Execution (Locally)

| test | command | report | verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unit | `cd code` `mvn clean verify -DskipITs -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false` | `code/jacoco-report-aggregate/target/site/jacoco-aggregate/index.html` | all tests pass and the **code coverage** generated by **unit** tests is at least **90%** |
| mutation | `cd code` `mvn clean verify pitest:mutationCoverage pitest:report-aggregate-module -DskipITs` | `code/target/pit-reports/index.html` | all tests pass and the **mutation coverage** is at least **90%** |
| integration | `cd code` `mvn clean verify -DskipUTs -DfailIfNoTests=false -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false` | `code/jacoco-report-aggregate/target/site/jacoco-aggregate-it/index.html` | all tests pass and the **code coverage** generated by **integration** tests is at least **80%** |

Table 2. Tests Execution (Github)

| test | command | report | verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unit | - workflow dispatch - automatically on PR | workflow execution reports | automatically on workflow execution |
| mutation | - workflow dispatch - automatically on PR | workflow execution reports | automatically on workflow execution |
| integration | - workflow dispatch - automatically on PR | workflow execution reports | automatically on workflow execution |
| compatibility | - workflow dispatch - automatically on PR | workflow execution reports | automatically on workflow execution |

# Docs module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/docs/

The documentation module `karatetools-oss-docs` follows standard structure for Antora documentation:

```
docs
├── antora-playbook.yml (1)
├── antora-playbook.local.yml (1)
├── .release-version (2)
├── node_modules (3)
├── package-lock.json (4)
├── package.json (4)
├── scripts (5)
├── src (6)
│   ├── antora.yml (7)
│   └── modules (8)
│       ├── ROOT
│       └── main
└── supplemental-ui (9)
```

| **1** | Antora playbooks — the real one, and the one used for local development and PR verification. |
| --- | --- |
| **2** | Plain-text file holding the next release’s target version, read by the release workflow. |
| **3** | Node modules folder. |
| **4** | Node package configuration file. |
| **5** | Helper scripts (e.g. check-links.mjs). |
| **6** | Content source root folder. |
| **7** | `antora.yml` (reserved file name): Antora component version descriptor file. This file indicates to Antora that the contents of a directory named `modules` should be collected and processed. |
| **8** | `modules` (reserved directory name): Antora required directory located at the same hierarchical level as the `antora.yml` file — `ROOT` (the home page only) and `main` (every other page). |
| **9** | Supplemental UI assets (logo, favicon) layered on top of the docouture UI bundle. |

To locally build the documentation, you can use the following commands from the `docs` directory:

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

This starts `docouture dev`, which builds the site and serves it at `http://localhost:5000` with live reload — pass `--port` to use a different one. See [Development](../../../development/) for the full command set (`docouture build`, `docouture doctor`, releasing, publishing).

# Karate test module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/karate-test/

This module `karatetools-oss-karate-test` is a **karate module** to **test** the **karate tools**.

- This module has been generated using the [⚙️ Karate Tools - Archetype](../../../guides/archetype/overview/)
- Includes auto-generated tests and mocks for sample api (`karatetools-oss-openapi-test`)
- uses the `karatetools-oss-starter` to test the karate clients and the sample application (`karatetools-oss-boot`) and containers.

> **Important**
> Any changes made in the Karate Tools **codebase** must be reflected in the corresponding **karate tests** in this module.

The structure of the module is as follows:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- **src/test/java**: Java Code ``` e2e/karate/ ├── .gitignore ├── pom.xml └── src └── test ├── java │ └── com │ └── inditextech │ └── karate │ └── karatetools │ ├── jms │ │ └── JMSKarateObject.java (1) │ └── test │ └── KarateRunnerTest.java (2) ``` | **1** | JMS Object for testing purposes | | --- | --- | | **2** | Java Test Runner |
- **src/test/resources**: Base and Config files ``` e2e/karate/ ├── .gitignore ├── pom.xml └── src └── test └── resources ├── config (1) │ ├── db │ │ ├── mariadb-config-local.yml │ │ ├── mongodb-config-local.yml │ │ └── postgresql-config-local.yml │ ├── jms │ │ └── activemq-config-local.yml │ └── kafka │ ├── avro │ │ └── karate.avsc │ └── kafka-config-local.yml ├── config-local.yml (2) ├── config.yml (2) ├── jwt (3) │ ├── default-jwt.yml │ └── invalid-jwt.yml ├── karate-config.js (4) ├── logback-test-debug.xml (5) ├── logback-test.xml (5) └── mocks (6) └── templates └── standalone └── .gitkeep ``` | **1** | Karate clients config files (db, jms, kafka) | | --- | --- | | **2** | Configuration Files (general and environment specific) | | **3** | Karate Authentication JWT Files (default and test specific) | | **4** | Karate-config files | | **5** | logback configuration files | | **6** | karate mocks folder |

The tests to be executed are:

- **Karate Tests**: - Karate tests are used to test the karate tools in the context of a Karate project. - These tests are executed against the test application Rest Api and the `docker containers` provided by the `karatetools-oss-boot` module.

> **Important**
> Karate tests are required as status checks in the CI/CD pipeline pull request approval process. The **level of coverage for the karate tests must reach at least the defined threshold**.

| test | command | report | verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build app | `cd code` `mvn clean install -DskipTests -DskipITs -DskipUTs` | NA | no errors |
| Start app | `cd code` `APP_PORT=8888` `PROJECT_VERSION=$(mvn -q -Dexec.executable="echo" -Dexec.args='${project.version}' --non-recursive exec:exec)` `APP_PATH_TO_JAR=boot/target/karatetools-boot-$PROJECT_VERSION.jar` `APP_OPTIONS=--server.port=$APP_PORT` `java -jar "$APP_PATH_TO_JAR" "$APP_OPTIONS"` | NA | no errors |
| karate | `cd e2e/karate` `APP_PORT=8888` `mvn clean verify -DAPP_PORT=$APP_PORT -Dkarate.env=local -Dkarate.options="-t ~@mock.templates.inline -t ~@ignore" -Dkarate.report.options="--showLog true" -Dlogback.configurationFile=src/test/resources/logback-test-debug.xml` | `e2e/karate/target/karate-reports/karate-summary.html` | all tests pass |

# Repository structure

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/overview/

This library is a general purpose library that can be used by any Karate project.

The **Karate Tools** Open Source Repository is organized as follows:

- `code` - Karate Tools Open Source **codebase** with the corresponding **unit** and **integration tests** - 👩‍💻 [karatetools-oss-code](../code/)
- `e2e/karate` - Karate Tools Open Source **karate tests** - 🧪 [karatetools-oss-karate-test](../karate-test/)
- `docs` - Karate Tools Open Source **documentation** based on **asciidoc and antora** - 📄 [karatetools-oss-docs](../docs/)

```
├── code (1)
│   ├── archetype (2)
│   │   └── src
│   │       └── test
│   │           ├── java
│   │           └── resources
│   ...
│   └── starter (2)
├── docs (3)
│   ├── build (4)
│   ├── node_modules (4)
│   ├── src
│   │   └── modules (5)
│   │       ├── HOME
│   │       │   ├── images
│   │       │   └── pages
│   │       ...
│   │       └── release
│   └── supplemental-ui (6)
└── e2e
    └── karate (7)
        └── src
            └── test
                ├── java
                └── resources
```

| **1** | **codebase** root directory |
| --- | --- |
| **2** | **codebase** maven modules |
| **3** | **documentation** root directory |
| **4** | **documentation** build and node directories |
| **5** | **documentation** antora asciidoc modules |
| **6** | **documentation** antora UI assets (page templates, CSS, JavaScript, images, etc.) |
| **7** | **karate-test** maven module root directory |

The main `code` modules are:

- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-archetype`: **archetype** to generate a **karate project from scratch** with the necessary **configurations** and **utilities** for the execution of tests.
- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-clients`: **clients** to interact with **relational databases via JDBC (MariaDB and PostgreSQL)**, **MongoDB**, **Kafka** and **JMS (Active MQ and Rabbit MQ)**
- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-generators`: **generators** of **tests** from **Open API**
- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-runner`: **karate runner** and all related utilities (**authentication**, **JWT tokens**, **karate base configuration**, **karate utils**, **karate mocks**, **karate cache**, **karate results and reports**, …​)
- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-starter`: **starter** module to include the **generators**, **clients** and **runner** in a Karate project.

It includes test open api modules:

- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-openapi-test`: **Open API** test specifications for the **karate tools tests** with two sub-modules: - 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-xxx-api-rest-stable`: **api** to test the **test generation tools** - 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-xxx-external-api-rest-stable`: **api** to test the **mock generation tools**

It includes a spring boot module:

- 👩‍💻 `karatetools-oss-boot`: **spring boot application** with a simple **rest api** implementing the **Open API** test specification and **docker containers** to be used as target for the **karate tools tests** (runner, rest, auth, jdbc, mongodb, kafka, jms, …​)

The karate test module is defined in the `e2e/karate` folder:

- 🧪 `karatetools-oss-karate-test`: **karate module** to **test** the **karate tools**. - This module has been generated using the [⚙️ Karate Tools - Archetype](../../../guides/archetype/overview/) - Includes auto-generated tests and mocks for sample api (`karatetools-oss-openapi-test`) - uses the `karatetools-oss-starter` to test the karate clients and the sample application (`karatetools-oss-boot`) and containers.

The documentation is defined in the `docs` folder:

- 📄 `karatetools-oss-docs`: **documentation** of the **karate tools** based on **asciidoc and antora**.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Runner module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/runner/

The `karatetools-oss-runner` module includes the following packages:

- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.jwt`: **JWT generator** to create **JWT tokens** for **authentication** and **authorization** purposes in **Karate** tests.
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.results`: **results generators** to **aggregate** the **cucumber results** of the **test scenarios**, to **create statistics** on the **karate operations usage** and to **copy the junit reports** to the **surefire folder**.
- 📦 `dev.inditex.karate.test`: **karate runner** to **run** the **karate tests** and **karate cache** to **share variables** across tests.

It also includes the following karate resources:

- 📜 `karate-base.js`: **karate base configuration**
- 📜 `karate-utils.js`: **karate tools utility js functions**
- `karate-auth` (`basic`, `jwt`): - 📜 `karate-auth.feature`: **common features** to connect to authentication services. - 📜 `karate-auth.js`: **karate auth functions** to orquestrate the **authentication** and **authorization** process.
- `mocks`: - 📜 `mock-templates.feature`: **common feature** to launch the **mocks**. - 📜 `mock-templates-functions.js`: **karate mocks functions** to find, load, …​ the **mock templates**. - 📜 `mock-templates-inline.feature`: **feature** to launch the **mocks** in **inline** mode. - 📜 `mock-templates-standalone.feature`: **feature** to launch the **mocks** in **standalone** mode.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Starter module

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/contributing/repo-structure/starter/

The `karatetools-oss-starter` module is a `packaging` module that includes the dependencies needed for a karate project to be able to use the karate tools, `karatetools-oss-clients`, `karatetools-oss-generators` and `karatetools-oss-runner` modules as well as any other necessary dependencies.

---

# Archetype

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/guides/archetype/overview/

The **Karate Tools Archetype** generates a karate project from scratch with the necessary configurations and utilities for the generation and execution of karate tests.

## 1. Note down the target artifact’s group ID, version and main package.

In the **artifact’s main `pom.xml`** file, you will find the artifact’s **group ID** and **version** for which the Karate tests are to be created.

```
  <groupId>com.mypackage</groupId>
  <version>X.X.X</version>
```

In the **artifact’s code**, you will find the artifact’s main package.

```
package com.mypackage;
```

## 2. Create a Karate project using the Karate Tools Archetype

Go to the folder where you want to create the karate project, for example `e2e` and run the following command:

```
mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeGroupId={karatetools-package} -DarchetypeArtifactId=karatetools-archetype -DinteractiveMode=true -DaskForDefaultPropertyValues=true -DarchetypeVersion={karatetools-version}
```

It will prompt for the **standard archetype properties**:

```
Define value for property 'groupId' com.mypackage: :
Define value for property 'artifactId' karate: :
Define value for property 'version' 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT: :
Define value for property 'package' com.mypackage.karate: :
```

For the generated karate project we **recommend to use**:

- Same **group ID** as the target artifact.
- **artifact ID**: `karate`
- Same **version** as the target artifact.
- **package** with the same value as the target artifact with suffix `.karate`, for example: `com.mypackage.karate`

It will prompt (**yes/no**) for the properties to include sample configuration files for the **Karate Clients** (**JDBC**, **MongoDB**, **Kafka** and **JMS**):

- **JDBC** - `includeJDBCClient_MariaDB` to include MariaDB JDBC client configuration - `includeJDBCClient_PostgreSQL` to include PostgreSQL JDBC client configuration
- **MongoDB** - `includeMongoDBClient` to include MongoDB configuration
- **Kafka** - `includeKafkaClients` to include Kafka configuration(s).
- **JMS** - `includeJMSClient_ActiveMQ` to include ActiveMQ configuration - `includeJMSClient_RabbitMQ` to include RabbitMQ configuration

```
Define value for property 'includeJDBCClient_MariaDB' yes: :
Define value for property 'includeJDBCClient_PostgreSQL' yes: :
Define value for property 'includeMongoDBClient' yes: :
Define value for property 'includeKafkaClients' yes: :
Define value for property 'includeJMSClient_ActiveMQ' yes: :
Define value for property 'includeJMSClient_RabbitMQ' yes: :
```

> **Tip**
> For a client not to be included type `n` or `no`, if it’s left empty it takes the default value.

This will automatically create the karate artifact folder structure, the test runner, the configuration and support files.

![archetype execution](../../../_images/archetype/archetype-execution.png)

```
  <groupId>com.mypackage</groupId>
  <artifactId>karate</artifactId>
  <version>X.X.X</version>
```

```
package com.mypackage.karate;
```

## 3. Review Karate project structure

![archetype output](../../../_images/archetype/archetype-output.png)

1. Tools version manager file: - .tool-versions
2. Git Ignore file: - .gitingore
3. Karate pom file: - pom.xml
4. Java Test Runner: - src/test/java/com/mypackage/karate/KarateRunnerTest.java
5. Configuration Files (general and environment specific): - src/test/resources/config.yml - src/test/resources/config-<env>.yml
6. Karate-config files: - src/test/resources/karate-config.js
7. Karate Authentication Default JWT: - src/test/resources/jwt/default-jwt.yml
8. logback configuration: - src/test/resources/logback-test.xml
9. karate clients configuration files as per archetype properties (includeJDBCClient_MariaDB, …​) - src/test/resources/config/db - src/test/resources/config/jms - src/test/resources/config/kafka
10. karate mocks folder to define standalone mock templates - src/test/resources/mocks/templates/standalone

## 4. Configure the artifact to include the karate module in the release versioning process

> **Caution**
> These steps are to be performed at the **target artifact main pom level**, not at karate level.

1. Main artifact `pom.xml` ``` <modules> ... <!-- Module to create the karate release only --> <module>karate-release</module> </modules> ```
2. `karate-release/pom.xml` > **Note** > The **workingDirectory** defined in the plugins pom, must point to the relative path to the karate module, for example: `<workingDirectory>../../e2e/karate</workingDirectory>` ``` <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd"> <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion> <parent> <groupId>TO_BE_COMPLETED</groupId> <artifactId>TO_BE_COMPLETED</artifactId> <version>TO_BE_COMPLETED</version> <relativePath>..</relativePath> </parent> <artifactId>karate-release</artifactId> <packaging>pom</packaging> <name>${project.groupId}:${project.artifactId}</name> <description /> <properties> <exec-maven-plugin.version>3.1.0</exec-maven-plugin.version> <maven-scm-plugin.version>2.2.1</maven-scm-plugin.version> </properties> <build> <plugins> <plugin> <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId> <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId> <version>${exec-maven-plugin.version}</version> <executions> <execution> <id>sync-karate-version</id> <goals> <goal>exec</goal> </goals> <configuration> <executable>mvn</executable> <workingDirectory>../../e2e/karate</workingDirectory> <arguments> <argument>org.codehaus.mojo:versions-maven-plugin:set</argument> <argument>-DnewVersion=${project.version}</argument> </arguments> </configuration> </execution> </executions> </plugin> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-scm-plugin</artifactId> <version>${maven-scm-plugin.version}</version> <executions> <execution> <id>sync-karate-version</id> <phase>default-cli</phase> <goals> <goal>add</goal> </goals> <configuration> <workingDirectory>../../e2e/karate</workingDirectory> <includes>pom.xml</includes> </configuration> </execution> </executions> </plugin> </plugins> </build> <profiles> <!-- Synchronizes karate versions with POM version --> <profile> <id>release-prepare</id> <build> <plugins> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-scm-plugin</artifactId> <executions> <execution> <id>sync-karate-version</id> <phase>process-sources</phase> </execution> </executions> </plugin> <plugin> <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId> <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId> <executions> <execution> <id>sync-karate-version</id> <phase>initialize</phase> </execution> </executions> </plugin> </plugins> </build> </profile> </profiles> </project> ```
3. Update the `maven-release-plugin` plugin in the **main pom** to execute the karate versioning ``` <build> <plugins> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-release-plugin</artifactId> ... <configuration> ... <!-- Karate release --> <preparationGoals>-Prelease-prepare clean verify</preparationGoals> <completionGoals>-pl karate-release exec:exec@sync-karate-version scm:add@sync-karate-version</completionGoals> </configuration> </plugin> </plugins> </build> ```

# Karate Clients - JDBC

Source: /karatetools-oss/prerelease/main/guides/clients/jdbc/

Java Client to interact with DataBases using **JDBC from karate**.

It provides features to execute SQL **queries**, SQL **inserts, updates, deletes, …​** and SQL **scripts from file**.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- How to set it up: - Define (if applicable) the JDBC client dependencies in the project **[POM](#pom-configuration)** - Define the JDBC client configuration in the file **[src/test/resources/config/db/<db-driver>-<env>-config.yml](#client-configuration)**
- How to use it in the karate files: - **[JDBC Client Features and Usage](#client-features-and-usage)**

The included JDBC Drivers are:

                    ...
                    postgresql-config-pre.yml
```

### JDBC Client Configuration Properties

⚙️ **`jdbc-url`** - JDBC URL to connect to the data base. JDBC URL is database specific.

- `jdbc:[protocol]//[host]:[port]/[database][?properties]`

⚙️ **`driver-class-name`** - JDBC Driver Class Name.

⚙️ **`username`** - user name to connect

⚙️ **`password`** - password to connect

⚙️ **`health-query`** - SQL query to use to check if the DB is available.

### JDBC Client Configuration Properties - MariaDB

Example

```
# docker-compose environment variables:  NA
# docker-compose folder structure:       mariadb/<DB_NAME>/scripts
jdbc-url: jdbc:mariadb://localhost:3306/KARATE
driver-class-name: org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver
username: karate
password: karate-pwd
health-query: SELECT 1 FROM DUAL
```

### JDBC Client Configuration Properties - PostgreSQL

## Client Features and Usage

### Instantiate JDBCClient

**New instance of the JDBCClient** providing the configuration as a map loaded from a yaml file.

Java Signature

```
public JDBCClient(final Map<Object, Object> configMap)
```

Gherkin Usage

```
# public JDBCClient(final Map<Object, Object> configMap)
# Instantiate JDBCClient
Given def config = read('classpath:config/db/postgresql-config-' + karate.env + '.yml')
Given def JDBCClient = Java.type('dev.inditex.karate.db.JDBCClient')
Given def jdbcClient = new JDBCClient(config)
```

### Check if JDBC is available

Checks if the **JDBC connection can be established** using the configured **health query**

Returns true is **connection is available**, false otherwise

Java Signature

```
public Boolean available()
```

Gherkin Usage

```
# public Boolean available()
When def available = jdbcClient.available()
Then if (!available) karate.fail('JDBC Client not available')
```

### Execute JDBC Update Script from file

Execute a **set of SQL update statements** (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, …​) **defined in a file**, each executable SQL line must end with the **separator ";"**. The separator can be ignored when executing each SQL depending on the DB, for example for DB2 ";" must be ignored.

Returns the **aggregated number of row count** for the executed SQL lines.

Java Signature

```
public int executeUpdateScript(final String script, final boolean ignoreSeparator)
```

Gherkin Usage

```
# public int executeUpdateScript(final String script, final boolean ignoreSeparator)
# Truncate Table and Insert 2 records
Given def scriptSQL = karate.readAsString('classpath:scenarios/db/JDBCClient-PostgreSQL.sql')
When def insertedScript = jdbcClient.executeUpdateScript(scriptSQL, false)
Then karate.log('jdbcClient.executeUpdateScript(',scriptSQL,')=',insertedScript)
Then assert insertedScript == 2
```

### Execute JDBC Update SQL

Execute a **single SQL update statement** (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, …​).

Returns the **row count** for the executed SQL statement or 0 for SQL statements that return nothing (such as TRUNCATE)

Java Signature

```
public int executeUpdate(final String sql)
```

Gherkin Usage

```
# public int executeUpdate(final String sql)
# Insert a record
Given def insertSQL = "INSERT INTO DATA (NAME, VALUE) VALUES ('karate-03', 3)"
When def inserted = jdbcClient.executeUpdate(insertSQL)
Then karate.log('jdbcClient.executeUpdate(',insertSQL,')=',inserted)
Then assert inserted == 1
```

### Execute JDBC Query SQL

Executes a **single SQL query statement**,

Returns a **JSON Array** representing the obtained ResultSet, where each row is a map **<< column name, ResultSet value >>**

For example:

```
SELECT ID, NAME, VALUE FROM DATA ORDER BY ID

ID|NAME     |VALUE|
--+---------+-----+
 1|karate-01|    1|
 2|karate-02|    2|
 3|karate-03|    3|
```

will return

```
[
  { "ID": 1, "NAME": "karate-01", "VALUE": 1 },
  { "ID": 2, "NAME": "karate-02", "VALUE": 2 },
  { "ID": 3, "NAME": "karate-03", "VALUE": 3 }
]
```

Java Signature

```
public List<Map<String, Object>> executeQuery(final String sql)
```

Gherkin Usage

```
# public List<Map<String, Object>> executeQuery(final String sql)
# Select inserted records
Given def selectSQL = "SELECT ID, NAME, VALUE FROM DATA ORDER BY VALUE ASC";
When def result = jdbcClient.executeQuery(selectSQL)
Then karate.log('jdbcClient.executeQuery(',selectSQL,')#=',result.length)
Then karate.log('jdbcClient.executeQuery(',selectSQL,')=',result)
Then assert result.length == 3
Then match result[0].id == '#notnull'
Then match result[0].name == 'karate-01'
Then match result[0].value == 1
Then match result[1].id == '#notnull'
Then match result[1].name == 'karate-02'
Then match result[1].value == 2
Then match result[2].id == '#notnull'
Then match result[2].name == 'karate-03'
Then match result[2].value == 3
```

### Apache Active MQ Config

⚙️ **`jmsFactory`** - JMS Factory to use: **`ActiveMQ`**

⚙️ **`brokerURL`** - URL of the Active MQ broker

⚙️ **`username`** - User name that the application uses to connect to ActiveMQ

⚙️ **`password`** - Password that the application uses to connect to ActiveMQ

⚙️ **`sendTimeout`** - Timeout in milliseconds for sending messages (default 5000)

Example

```
# docker-compose environment variables:  <AMQ_USER> <AMQ_PASSWORD>
# docker-compose folder structure:       NA
jmsFactory: ActiveMQ
brokerURL: tcp://localhost:61616
username: karate
password: karate-pwd
```

### Rabbit MQ Config

⚙️ **`jmsFactory`** - JMS Factory to use: **`RabbitMQ`**

⚙️ **`host`** - RabbitMQ server host

⚙️ **`port`** - RabbitMQ server port

⚙️ **`username`** - User name that the application uses to connect to RabbitMQ

⚙️ **`password`** - Password that the application uses to connect to RabbitMQ

⚙️ **`virtual-host`** - virtual host to be used when creating a connection to RabbitMQ (default is "/")

⚙️ **`on-message-timeout`** - Timeout in milliseconds for processing messages (default 5000)

⚙️ **`amqp`** - When `true`, uses native AMQP destinations (default exchange routing) instead of JMS queues. ObjectMessage is not supported in AMQP mode - use Map or String payloads instead (default is `false`)

Example

```
# docker-compose environment variables:  <RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER> <RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS> <RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_VHOST>
# docker-compose folder structure:       NA
jmsFactory: RabbitMQ
# host: RabbitMQ server host.
host: localhost
# port: RabbitMQ server port.
port: 25672
# username: User name that the application uses to connect to RabbitMQ.
username: karate
# password: Password that the application uses to connect to RabbitMQ.
password: karate-pwd
# virtual-host: virtual host to be used when creating a connection to RabbitMQ.
virtual-host: /
# on-message-timeout: Timeout in milliseconds for processing messages.
on-message-timeout: 5000
```

### RabbitMQ AMQP mode

The RabbitMQ JMS client operates in two modes:

- **JMS mode** (`amqp: false`, default): Messages are routed through JMS-managed destinations (e.g., `jms.durable.queues` exchange). ObjectMessage payloads are serialized using Java serialization. This mode is compatible with other JMS clients consuming from the same queues.
- **AMQP mode** (`amqp: true`): Messages are sent as raw AMQP using the default exchange, which routes directly to queues by name. No JMS serialization layer is involved. Only TextMessage and BytesMessage are supported (ObjectMessage will throw a `JMSRuntimeException`).

Use **AMQP mode** when the application under test uses **native AMQP** rather than JMS to interact with RabbitMQ. Common cases include:

- **Spring Cloud Stream** applications bound to RabbitMQ - these publish and consume raw AMQP messages, not JMS-serialized ones.
- Applications using the **native RabbitMQ client** (`com.rabbitmq:amqp-client`) directly.
- Any framework that interacts with RabbitMQ via the AMQP 0-9-1 protocol without a JMS layer.

If the application under test uses the **RabbitMQ JMS client** (`com.rabbitmq.jms:rabbitmq-jms`) to produce and consume messages, use **JMS mode** (the default).

> **Note**
> When targeting a Spring Cloud Stream consumer, you must also set the `contentType` JMS property (e.g., `{'contentType': 'application/json'}`) so that Spring can deserialize the message payload correctly.

### Send a message to a queue

**Send a message to a queue**

For example:

JMS Text Message - JSON

```
Given def jmsMessageJSON = {'id': '1', 'name': 'karate-01', 'value': 1}
```

JMS Text Message - Plain Text

```
Given def jmsMessagePlainText = 'Plain Text Message'
```

JMS Text Message - XML

```
Given text jmsMessageXML =
"""
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<karate id="1">
  <name>karate-01</name>
  <value>1</value>
</karate>
"""
```

> **Important**
> In order for an XML to be sent as JMS Text Message you need to use `text` (with enclosed content `"""`) instead of `def` (`def` converts to Map anything that looks like JSON/XML).

JMS Object Message

```
Given def JMSKarateObject = Java.type('dev.inditex.karate.jms.JMSKarateObject')
Given def jmsMessageObject = new JMSKarateObject("2", "karate-02", 2)
```

> **Important**
> When using RabbitMQ in AMQP mode (`amqp: true` in config), **ObjectMessage is not supported**. Use JSON Map, Plain Text, or XML payloads instead. Attempting to send an ObjectMessage in AMQP mode will throw a `JMSRuntimeException`.

Java Signature

```
public void send(final String queue, final Object value)
```

Gherkin Usage - JMS Text Message - JSON

```
# Define Queue
Given def queue = 'global.core.karate.public.queue'

# public void send(final String queue, final Object value)
# Send Message without properties
Given def jmsMessageJSON = {'id': '1', 'name': 'karate-01', 'value': 1}
When jmsClient.send(queue, jmsMessageJSON)
```

Gherkin Usage - JMS Text Message - Plain Text

```
# Define Queue
Given def queue = 'global.core.karate.public.queue'

# public void send(final String queue, final Object value)
# Send Message without properties

```

Gherkin Usage - JMS Text Message - XML

```

# public void send(final String queue, final Object value)
# Send Message without properties

"""
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<karate id="1">
  <name>karate-01</name>
  <value>1</value>
</karate>
"""

```

### Consume Messages from a queue

**Receive the next messages in the queue** within the default timeout interval (5000ms) or custom timeout interval.

Returns a **JSON Array** representing the obtained messages, where each row is a map **<< field name, message value >>**

For example:

JSON or Object Messages

```
[
  { "id": 1, "name": "karate-01", "value": 1 },
  { "id": 2, "name": "karate-02", "value": 2 }
]
```

Plain Text or XML Messages

```
[
  { "textMessage": "Plain Text Message" },
  { "textMessage": "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<karate id=\"1\">\n  <name>karate-01</name>\n  <value>1</value>\n</karate>" }
]
```

Java Signature

```
public List<Map<String, Object>> consume(final String queue)
```

Gherkin Usage - JSON or Object Messages

```
# Define Queue
Given def queue = 'global.core.karate.public.queue'

# public List<Map<String, Object>> consume(final String queue)
When def messages = jmsClient.consume(queue)
Then karate.log('messages=', messages)
Then assert messages.length == 2
Then def result = karate.sort(messages, x => x.id)
Then match result[0].id == '1'
Then match result[0].name == 'karate-01'
Then match result[0].value == 1
Then match result[1].id == '2'
Then match result[1].name == 'karate-02'
Then match result[1].value == 2
```

```
